item.title: Council says it plans to review off-street car parking in Killorglin town
item.description: Kerry County Council says it plans to review off-street car parking in Killorglin town. The information was provided in response to a motion from Independent councillor Podge Foley at the recent meeting of Kenmare Municipal District. Cllr Foley sough an update on the status of off-street parking in the town, in particular at the courthouse car park. item.title: Kerry marked for new recycling hubs as part of circular economy strategy
item.description: Tralee or Killarney will be the location for the county's new reuse, repair and recyling hubs. That's according to Minister of State Alan Dillon who was speaking regarding the launch of the country's new circular economy strategy. Part of this will include support to local authorities to develop reuse, repair, and recycling hubs nationwide. item.title: Director of SouthDoc welcomes funding for Killarney Local Injury Unit
item.description: The director of SouthDoc has welcomed the announcement of funding for a local injury unit in Killarney. Over €840,000 (€842,100) has been assigned for the appraisal stage of the proposed unit in Killarney, under the HSE’s newest capital plan. The unit will focus on minor injuries like fractures, sprains, and burns, to reduce pressure on University Hospital Kerry (UHK). item.title: Castleisland educational publishing company launches new digital learning platform
item.description: A Castleisland educational publishing company has launced a new digital learning platform built for Irish classrooms. Educate.ie has launched EdPal, which has been developed specifically for Irish post-primary schools through direct collaboration with teachers. The end product is a structured platform alligned with the current school curriculums, including lesson delivery, student engagement, and assessment. item.title: Kerry County Council to receive over €1 million under Local Improvement Scheme
item.description: Kerry County Council is to receive over €1.1 million (€1,133,190) under this year’s Local Improvement Scheme. The Minister for Rural and Community Development, Dara Calleary, announced that the scheme will provide €17.55 million nationwide, up €2 million on last year. This funding will be used to repair non-public rural roads and laneways which provide access to rural homes and farms and are not normally maintained by the local authority. item.title: Taylor To Retire
item.description: Katie Taylor has revealed that she is set to retire with one more fight left on the cards. The legendary world champion boxer from Bray has confirmed that the fight will take place in Dublin this summer. Taylor has reiterated her desire to fight at Croke Park but has admitted she's unsure if that will happen. Advertisement The 3 Arena and the Aviva Stadium are the alternatives for the former Olympic champion.

item.title: Man charged and due before court in relation to Mike Gaine homicide investigation
item.description: A man has been charged and is due before the court in connection with the disappearance and homicide of Kenmare farmer Mike Gaine. 56-year-old Michael Gaine was first reported missing from his home near Kenmare on 21st March last year. Body tissue, confirmed to be his, was found after slurry was spread on Mike Gaine's land seven weeks later. item.title: Íarnród Éireann aiming to provide regular hourly service between Tralee and Mallow
item.description: Íarnród Éireann says its aim is to provide a regular hourly service between Tralee and Mallow. The rail operator announced that last year demand on the Tralee to Cork and Dublin services increased by more than eight per cent to over 962,000 journeys. Irish Rail says this is a record. Advertisement Barry Kenny is spokesperson for Íarnród Éireann. He says Kerry will benefit from a €1.8 billion investment in Cork’s commuter rail network. item.title: Michael Kelley appears in court charged with murder of Mike Gaine
item.description: American man Michael Kelley has appeared in court charged with the murder of Kenmare farmer Michael Gaine. 54-year-old Mr Kelley, who had been residing in Tralee, appeared in Tralee District Court, where he was remanded in custody. Mr Kelley faces one charge; that on a date unknown between 20th March 2025 and 21st March 2025, at Carrig, Kenmare, he murdered Michael Gaine, contrary to common law. item.title: Taoiseach apologises to institutional abuse survivors following hunger strike by Kerry group
item.description: The Taoiseach has apologised to survivors of institutional abuse. Mícheál Martin gave the apology in the Dáil after meeting with a group of survivors, some of whom were in reform and industrial schools in Kerry. The four had taken part in a 51-day hunger strike outside Leinster House late last year. Advertisement They had campaigned for improved supports for survivors.
